memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"Any male descendant of Aaron may eat it. For all generations to come it is his perpetual share of the food offerings presented to the LORD. Whatever touches them will become holy."'" - Lev 6:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Whatever touches them will become holy.

That last phrase is striking, and it runs in an unexpected direction. In much of Leviticus, contact with something unclean spreads uncleanness. Here, contact with something holy spreads holiness. The holy is contagious.

We must be careful not to overread this — in the ceremonial system it meant such items became consecrated to God's use, not that they became morally good. But the direction of the picture is remarkable, and it anticipates something.

Under the old covenant, holiness generally had to be protected from contamination. Then Jesus came, and something changed. He touched a leper, and instead of Jesus becoming unclean, the leper became clean (Mk 1:41-42). He touched a bier carrying a dead boy, and the boy lived (Lk 7:14-15). Uncleanness did not spread to Him. Wholeness spread from Him.

That is the direction the gospel runs. Christ's holiness is stronger than our contamination.

And Paul applies this to believers: an unbelieving husband is sanctified through his believing wife (1 Cor 7:14) — God's presence in one life spilling into a household.

You do not have to withdraw from the world to stay clean. Christ in you is the stronger influence.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I approach the world defensively, afraid of contamination?
2. Where might God want my presence to be an influence for good rather than a retreat?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You touched what was unclean and made it whole. Let Your presence in me be a blessing wherever You place me. Amen.
